finding: Reviewed seven banking-design and joint-linkage sources. Institutional comparison populations, structural exclusions, eligibility versus take-up and Bayesian linkage feedback remain explicit; no essential manuscript defect found in the indexed scopes.
next_action: Continue exact-reader Q2 from semantic-review-14.json with remaining econometric, statistical and frontier primary papers, then LLM and capability records. Preserve identified populations, version-specific scope and negative findings.

records.finding: Printed pages 2-3 compare eligible agency high-LTV loans with observationally similar ineligible non-agency loans, and explicitly distinguish selected refinancers from program-level differences including the extensive margin. The manuscript uses the design to motivate separate eligibility, application and closing records; it does not import household spending estimates as bank net value.

Section 4.2.1 equations (6)-(8) use premove bank market share as an instrument for existing deposit relationships among municipality movers, with current market share in the control set, alongside tenure analyses. The manuscript accurately preserves the mover population and treats the former-availability exclusion as substantive, not a universal instrument recipe.

The primary manuscript combines product and loan-amount demand with differentiated multiproduct lender pricing and uses predetermined risk-weighted capital requirements as cost shifters for endogenous rates. The proposal correctly presents this as a structural extension requiring additional exclusions, without inferring that general causal software already supplies the market-equilibrium model.

Printed pages 112-113 explicitly state that regional comparisons difference out common aggregate responses. The additional model introduces collateral constraints, cash-out refinancing and endogenous lender income/consumption. The proposal faithfully uses this to separate regional evidence from aggregate policy counterfactuals requiring further structure.

Printed pages 2-4 distinguish within-bank branch comparisons across local deposit concentration from within-county lending comparisons using bank-level exposure. Transfer of deposits across branches is an explicit identifying premise. The manuscript preserves both levels and limits the evidence to the deposits-channel mechanism, without assigning it to arbitrary household retention interventions.

Section III.B equation (5) introduces firm effects after first differencing to compare lending by different banks to the same firm. The saved 2006 text explicitly limits this to multiple-bank firms and discusses anticipatory adjustments and bank-specific demand correlated with funding shocks. The manuscript retains those restrictions and labels the version rather than substituting a later published design.

Section 2.3 equation (2.4) combines the one-to-one linkage constraint, agreement fields, linked outcome regression f1 and unlinked outcome distribution f2. Outcomes therefore affect posterior linkage odds under this joint model. All three manuscript contexts distinguish that feedback, prior and likelihood from independent-audit frequentist constructions and do not count posterior linkage draws as additional independent customers.
